title: Private GPU pool sizing: service classes, run-rate math, and egress constraints
text:
Private GPU pool sizing: service classes, run-rate math, and egress constraints

['From: Maria Le <maria.le@acmecloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer, laura_bennett
Cc: cloudops@partnercloud.io
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request: private GPU pool for Acme - throughput targets + egress

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. Our infra team needs a recommended run-rate and concrete sizing for a private (VPC) GPU pool Redwood would operate inside our account. High-level workload info below — can you validate assumptions and propose service-class sizing + egress numbers?

Workload summary:
- Steady-state: 3,600 inference requests/min (60 rps)
- Typical request size: 80 tokens output on average, model = Llama2-70B-quant (approx)
- Peak bursts: up to 30k requests/min (~500 rps) for 10–20 min windows during business events
- QoS target: P95 generation latency < 300ms; P99 < 800ms for small prompts
- Persistence: KV-cache beneficial for repeated prefixes (search / assistant sessions)
- Network constraints: our uplink to Redwood egress carriers is currently 20 Gbps per VPC segment

Questions:
1) How would you map requests into service classes (e.g., interactive vs batch vs background)?
2) For each class, what run-rate / GPU count do you recommend (assume A100-80 equivalence)?
3) What egress bandwidth budget should we reserve (Gbps) to avoid contention?
4) Any warm-pool / caching recommendations to hit the latency targets during bursts?

We want a concise sheet with numbers and assumptions so Procurement can budget. Also please attach any run-rate math.

Thanks,
Maria
Infrastructure Programs — Acme Cloud Retail

Maria — thanks, this is a great brief. I sketched a service-class proposal and run-rate math (attached). High level below; the attachment (run-rate-sheets.xlsx) contains the per-GPU concurrency assumptions and token math.

Quick proposal (assume A100-80 equivalency, 1 GPU ~ 18 concurrent interactive sessions at your 80-token average with our inference stack + quantization profile):

Service classes and sizing:
- Interactive (S1): low-latency assistant sessions; target steady 60 rps, burst to 250 rps
  - Recommended capacity: 6 GPUs active, 2-GPU warm spare (total 8 in cluster)
- High-throughput bursts (S2): event-driven bursts; absorbed by autoscale to 24 GPUs (warm pool 6) to reach ~500 rps at burst peak
- Background / batch (S3): offline reranking / embeddings; 4 dedicated GPUs, scheduled windows to avoid egress collision

Why these numbers:
- Per-GPU concurrency = 18 for 80-token completions (we benchmarked this on 80B quantized model on A100-class); sustained tokens/sec and KV cache hit-rate materially change throughput — see sheet for sensitivity.
- Autoscale policy: keep warm pool sized for 95th percentile short bursts (6 GPUs) and ramp to target within 90s via prefetch + container start optimization.

Network / egress budget:
- Baseline egress per 1 rps with 80 tokens out ~= 12 KB (serialized); at 500 rps that’s ~6 MB/s =~ 48 Mbps — this is small per se, but with many concurrent clients and large latent inputs we recommend budgeting headroom.
- Suggested reservation: 5 Gbps per cluster for steady+bursts, plus an additional 5 Gbps reserved for background transfers and model downloads (total 10 Gbps). If you have multi-cluster sprawl, multiply accordingly.

Warm-pool & caching:
- KV prefix cache recommended for assistant flows — set per-tenant cache TTL 15m with pre-warm hooks during predicted event windows.
- Keep ~25% of capacity as warm to absorb cold-start jitter; enable eager model mmap to reduce container spin up time.

Attachments: run-rate-sheets.xlsx (detailed math), network-egress-summary.pdf (bandwidth calc), sizing-proposal-v1.pptx (slides).

Next steps:
- Laura / Jonas: can you review the GPU counts for operational feasibility in the VPC and confirm any hard limits?
- Maria: if this looks directionally correct I can produce a one-page SLA + costing stub for Procurement.

- Karthik
Head of Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Looping back with operational notes and agreed action items. Summary of what we'll deliver by EOD Thursday:

- Karthik: finalize the one-page sizing + cost bands (steady vs peak) and include assumptions for per-GPU concurrency and token math. Attach to DocuSign packet for Procurement.
- Laura: validate VPC limits and confirm whether Acme's 20 Gbps link requires regional peering or can be handled via private interconnect. If we need >10 Gbps per cluster we should propose multi-AZ clusters.
- Vanessa: draft the security attestation (SOC2 reference + KMS integration bullets).
- Maria / Acme: please confirm whether bursts will come from a single region or multiple regions — that affects egress budgeting.

Notes: we will recommend an initial deployment of 8 GPUs (6 active + 2 warm) in region-us-west2, with autoscale ceiling at 30 GPUs (24 for burst + 6 warm). This keeps container churn controlled while meeting your P95 targets given caching. If egress proves tighter than expected we have a staged plan to prioritize interactive traffic on private interconnect and schedule background jobs outside peak windows.
